name: Thalamic Environmental Filtering (Pulvinar)
higher_order_principle: The pulvinar nucleus acts as a dynamic filter on environmental information reaching cortex, implementing attentional modes (focused 'spotlight' vs distributed 'floodlight') that are selected by spatial configuration (e.g., corridor vs atrium) and modulated by top-down goals.
scope_conditions: Applies to sighted individuals in illuminated environments
Top-down goals can override spatial layout cues
Pulvinar integrates cross-modal info, not just visual
moderators: developmental_status (children may default to floodlight due to immature pulvinar)

interactions.description: T46 specifies the thalamic mechanism determining HOW attention (T4) is deployed.
Pulvinar gates at the relay level; Acetylcholine (T26) modulates gain at the cortical level.

key_references: Saalmann, Y. B., & Kastner, S. (2011). Cognitive and perceptual functions of the visual thalamus. Neuron.
Saalmann, Y. B., et al. (2012). The pulvinar regulates information transmission between cortical areas. Science.
